Hi Evelyn —

Thanks again for your time today. Great to meet you and see the Acme Analytics use cases — the real-time insights demo was helpful context. Per our call you mentioned a couple of security/compliance items to validate before procurement: SOC 2 status, GDPR/HIPAA considerations, and specifically encryption/key management and whether customer-managed keys are supported.

Quick recap and proposed next steps:
- We are SOC 2 Type II compliant (certificate and summary available) — I can share the report stub and an overview PDF.
- Encryption: all customer data is encrypted in-transit (TLS 1.2+/mTLS options for ingest endpoints) and at-rest using AES-256.
- KMS/Customer-managed keys: Redwood supports customer-managed keys via integrations with AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, and Azure Key Vault. We support envelope encryption and BYOK (bring-your-own-key) flows; keys can be rotated per customer policy and we provide audit logs for key usage.
- HSM: for customers requiring HSM-backed key storage we support KMS-backed HSMs via the cloud providers; for private/on-prem deployments we can integrate with customer HSMs (PKCS#11) as part of the deployment package.

Can I loop in our sales engineer to provide a concise vendor security questionnaire response and share the SOC 2 doc + a KMS architecture diagram? If there are HIPAA-specific controls you need called out, please list them and we’ll highlight those items in the questionnaire response.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll share the SOC 2 summary + KMS diagram and a preliminary answers doc (attached stub).
2) Aditya (SE) will follow up with technical details for the questionnaire and confirm BYOK/HSM options for your environment.
3) If useful, we can schedule a 30-min technical call with your security team next week.

Are you available Wednesday (3/11) 10–11am PT or Thursday (3/12) 9–10am PT?

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Evelyn / Marissa —

Thanks — I’m available Wed 3/11 10am PT and will join the call. Below are concise answers to the specific KMS/BYOK/HSM questions to help your security review and to seed the vendor questionnaire. I’ll also upload a filled questionnaire draft to the Drive link and attach the SOC 2 summary + KMS diagram (stubs).

KMS / encryption highlights (hosted API):
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ with forward secrecy. Option to require mTLS for dedicated customer endpoints.
- At-rest: All customer data stored on encrypted volumes (AES-256). We use envelope encryption: data keys are wrapped with a customer master key (CMK) stored in the cloud KMS.
- Supported KMS providers: AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault. For hosted customers we can accept customer-managed keys (CMKs) where you provide the key in your cloud project/account and grant Redwood a usage IAM role to call Encrypt/Decrypt.
- BYOK lifecycle: For hosted deployments we require the customer to create and own the CMK in their cloud account. The customer controls creation, rotation, and destruction. Redwood does not store plaintext CMKs or key material. We request an IAM role with Encrypt/Decrypt permissions only; key rotation is handled by the customer and Redwood will continue using the current key ARN/ID.
- Key usage logging: All key operations are routed through the cloud KMS and will appear in the provider’s KMS audit logs (CloudTrail/Cloud Audit Logs/Azure Monitor). We surface key usage events in our audit logs and can produce per-request key IDs in our logs for correlation.
- HSM/backed keys: If you require HSM-backed keys, you can provision an HSM-backed CMK in your cloud KMS (AWS KMS with AWS CloudHSM, etc.) or we can integrate with a customer HSM in Private/Dedicated deployments (PKCS#11).

Differences by deployment mode:
- Hosted API: BYOK supported via customer-owned CMKs in your cloud account. Redwood holds no key material and only requests Encrypt/Decrypt permissions.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): similar BYOK flow; options to deploy in your cloud account for additional isolation.
- Private / On-prem: keys can be controlled entirely by you (HSM/PKCS#11) and integrated during deployment; Redwood’s control plane can be deployed in your VPC with no key material leaving your environment.

HIPAA / BAA: Redwood has a BAA template and will sign for customers who require HIPAA coverage. The BAA scopes hosted and dedicated deployments where we process PHI; private on-prem deployments are handled case-by-case. Our SOC 2 report documents security controls; we will call out HIPAA-specific control mappings in the questionnaire. Legal can engage once you confirm desire to proceed.

Attachments I’m uploading to the shared Drive and attaching here as stubs: SOC2-report-2025-summary.pdf, KMS-architecture-diagram.png, redwood-vendor-security-questionnaire-response.docx (draft). Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xYz-Redwood-Security-Docs
